children: Average engine power has risen 28.9 per cent in 20 years as automakers use turbocharging and hybrid technology to improve performance

Car engines are getting smaller, but they are delivering more power. Average engine power has increased 28.9 per cent over the past 20 years to 148 brake horsepower (bhp), according to an analysis by Vehicle Data Global (VDG), a vehicle data technology company.
The findings show how automakers are using turbocharging and hybrid technology to improve performance while meeting stricter emission standards.

VDG found that average engine capacity fell from 1,771cc in 2005 to 1,633cc in 2025, a decline of 7.8 per cent. At the same time, average power produced per litre of engine capacity rose 42.9 per cent to 69.1 kilowatts per litre.
This means smaller engines can now deliver power that was once associated with sports cars and performance models.

Cars producing at least 134bhp from engines of 1.5 litres or less have become far more common. According to VDG, registrations of these cars increased from 8,500 in 2005 to 4,44,000 in 2025. Their share of total registrations rose from 0.4 per cent to 26.7 per cent.
The analysis cites the Skoda Octavia 1.5 TSI e-TEC mild hybrid as an example of a modern car delivering power comparable to performance models from the 1990s, despite having a smaller engine.
The Nissan Qashqai 1.3 DIG-T mild hybrid is another example, producing more power than the classic Triumph TR6 PI, according to the study.
VDG clarified that the power figures for hybrid vehicles include the contribution from electric motors, rather than measuring output from the combustion engine alone.

Smaller engines also became more popular over the years. The share of cars with 1.0-litre engines rose from around 3.3 per cent of registrations in 2005 to 18 per cent in 2020. It stood at 14.5 per cent in 2025.

However, the shift towards smaller engines now appears to be slowing. Average engine capacity declined only slightly, from around 1,645cc in 2019 to 1,633cc in 2025. Average power, meanwhile, increased from 105kW to 111kW.
